Question 8 Remarkable Phosphorus Heterocycles
Introductory heterocyclic chemistry most often focuses on N, O, and S heteroatoms. Phosphorus, however, has a large valence-shell space and a rich range of coordination numbers and oxidation states. It can form low-coordinate λ species as well as hypercoordinate $\lambda^5$ species, where λ denotes the number of bonds to P. Phosphorus heterocycles exhibit remarkable structures and properties and are uniquely valuable in studies of low-valent metal ligands and tunable fluorophores. (Stereochemistry need not be considered in this problem.)

8.3 Phosphenium ions are often regarded as cationic heavy-element analogs of carbenes, but extending classical carbocation rearrangements such as the Wagner–Meerwein rearrangement directly to phosphorus chemistry remains challenging. Researchers proposed that a carbocation generated adjacent to P in a phosphirane might rearrange to a phosphenium ion, opening a new ring-forming pathway. In this problem, $W(CO)_5$ coordinated to P does not participate directly in the transformations.
